LESSON: WEAVING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.5: Weaving
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Weaving, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: Why is recycling beneficial to the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Weaving together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: will be developed as the learner weave a mat/scarf using a 2/2 plain weave on a

serrated card loom.

• Creativity and imagination: The learner comes up with new ideas on how to make a loom

Values:
• Responsibility: as learners put into practise the aspects of safety, care of the environment while sourcing for materials for

weaving.

• Respect: is nurtured when the learner appreciates and appraises others’ woven items

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: The learner observes safety as they perform rolls, balances and cartwheel to form a 3-phase sequence of a gymnastic

performance

18

• Climate change: The learner uses materials that are friendly to the environment when improvising the yarns and loom for

weaving

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: The learner creates a loom frame using a mitre joint while applying mathematical knowledge on angles.

Suggested learning resources

Recyclable yarns, fibres, cardboard, pieces of paper, cutting tools, video clips showing the weaving process withassistive

technologies for the hearing impaired
